records.source_notes: Third-order Birch-Murnaghan reference isotherm plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The room-temperature quench-data fit gives K0=221(2) GPa and K0'=3.3(1) with V0=328.4 A^3 fixed; those three reference parameters were then fixed in the P-V-T fit. The official supplement defines T0=298 K, theta0=1425 K, n=5 atoms per B4C formula unit, gamma(V)=gamma0*(V/V0)^q, and theta(V)=theta0*exp[(gamma0-gamma(V))/q]. A Peritheos P-V-T errors-in-variables refit with gamma0 fixed gives q=1.050(519), so it does not independently recover q=2.1; details and the primary-data transcription are in docs/literature-reproductions.md. The average disordered R-3m structure is diffraction-ready and is reported stable over the experimental range.

records.source_notes: This is the complete empirical pressure-scale form in Appendix B, not a standalone 300 K Vinet fit. Equation (3) and the three globally optimized coefficients define a zero-temperature cold Vinet curve; Equation (B2) adds an absolute thermal pressure that is nonzero at 300 K. The stored Tr=300 K is the Taylor expansion and operational increment reference, not the temperature of the cold curve. Tables II-III label compression by the ambient initial V0=1/rho0 from rho0=3.590 g/cm^3, whereas Equation (B2) defines eta with the smaller fitted cold V0K. The five new shock states span 152-265 GPa; the three reported temperatures span 3088-5676 K. The full quasi-Debye Helmholtz construction in Equations (1)-(6) is not independently reconstructable from the article because the numerical longitudinal- and shear-velocity versus density fits needed for the Debye-temperature law are not published. The authors therefore supply Equations (B1)-(B2) as the derived executable P-V-T form. No uncertainty confidence level or covariance is reported for the three optimized cold coefficients, and no errors are reported for c0-c5. The APS article record and full paper were checked; no official supplemental file or machine-readable data deposit is linked.
